slides.texte_overlay:
Small habits that make people
respect you instantly
Using people's names. "Thanks, Martin." It's simple, but it shows attention and respect, and people instantly feel more respect for you in return, every time.
Keeping your voice steady when things go wrong. A missed train, a late delivery, a mistake at work. Calm under small pressure earns big respect from everyone watching.
Not interrupting. Let people finish, even when you know what they're about to say. Patience in conversation is a sign of a man who is sure of himself.
Paying back money quickly. The lunch, the concert ticket, the taxi. Settling small debts the same day shows you can be trusted with much bigger things.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. People respect someone who keeps learning, and it shows in everything you say and do.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. People respect someone who keeps learning.

slides.texte_overlay: Standing up for someone who isn't there. When a group mocks an absent friend, say "Come on, he's a good guy." Loyalty like that is always noticed and remembered.
Keeping your word on time. If you say five minutes, it's five minutes. Respecting other people's time is the fastest way to be respected yourself, at work and at home.
